To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a bifunctional selenium-catalyzed strategy to synthesize trifluoromethythiolated tetrahydro-naphthalenes by combining desymmetrizations with trifluoromthyl-thiolation of gem-diaryl-tethers.
the catalytic asymmetric desymmetrizing sulfenylation of gem-diaryl-teth-ered alkenes and alkyne by using selenide catalysts has been realized for the first time.

a selenide-coupled bifunctional catalyst is developed for the first time to enable enantioselectivetrifluoromethythiolation of alkenes and diols by merging the desymmetrizaiton and trifluorothiolation strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the enantioselectivity of selenides and sulfides as chiral organocatalysts in the asymmetric desymmetrizing trifluoromethylation of gem-diaryl-tetrahydrofurans and gem-diaryl-tetracyclanes.
the enantioselectivity of the catalytic desymmetrizing trifluoromethylation of gem-diaryl-tetrahydronaphtalenes with trifluoromethylene-sulfuranes (Scheme 1).

the development of a new method for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of structurally and functionally diverse chiral trifluoro-methylthiolated compounds, which are an important class biologically active molecules.

this work represents the first example of a selenide-cata-lyzed desymmetrized sulfenylation of a C=C bond.

a novel and practical method for the catalytic enantiodivergent synthesis of various structurally complex trifluoromethanesulfenylated tetrahydropyran and tetrahydrothiophene derivatives has been developed by merging desym metrization and trif luoromethanesulphenylation.
the presented work provides a new approach for the catalytic enantioselctive synthesis of trifluroromethyltholated tetrahydornaphthalene derivatives.

we have developed a novel bifunctional selselide catalyzed approach for enantioselectivly synthesis of various chrial trifluoromethyithiolated molecules by merging desymmertrization and trifluromethythiolation.
we have developed a bifunctional selenium-catalyzed strategy for the enantioselectivetrifluoromethylation of alkenes and diols.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the selenide catalyst is superior to sulfide catalyst in the desymmetri-zation of gem-dialkyl-tethered alcohols and the sulfenylation of gem-dialkoxy-tethered aldehydes.

we can use selenide catalysts to catalyze enantioselectively the desymmetrizaiton and trifluorothiolation reaction of gem-daryl-tethered diols and dienes, and the products are obtained in excellent enantioselectivity.
the trifluoromethylation of sulfides can be achieved by using selenides as a catalyst, which is a novel catalytic system.
